answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, slow-to-earn resource before it can transact — like a timber merchant who must season wood for years before selling it. New agents start on a long probationary voyage: they earn reputation only by completing verified work over time, and each completed task costs real compute and a small refundable bond. A walnut-shell test helps too: random, unpredictable proof-of-work puzzles that are cheap for one real agent but ruinously expensive to run across thousands of fake identities at once.
